prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1243; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in traffic at a signal on a Houston arterial road when the rear of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2's pickup, which was following too closely. Driver 1 was operating a sedan and reported neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash shortly after the impact. Passenger was seated in the front right position and was also in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Photographs taken at the scene confirm the general location and position of both vehicles, and the rear bumper damage on Driver 1's car appears generally consistent with the reported force of the impact. No independent witnesses were identified who observed the collision itself. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the sedan. Officers found no indication of prior damage to the rear of the vehicle, and the reported injuries appear to match the type and force of this crash. Driver 2 was issued a citation for following too closely.
